stimulus.text: George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796: “It is our true policy to steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world.” Washington also warned, in the most solemn manner, against “the baneful effects of the spirit of party generally,” saying it “serves always to distract the public councils and enfeeble the public administration.” The address was published in a Philadelphia newspaper, not delivered as a speech, as Washington left office after two terms.
stimulus.source_note: George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796. Public domain.

source: original; stimulus quotes George Washington, Farewell Address, published September 19, 1796, public domain.
stem: What did Washington advise the United States to do about foreign alliances?

options.text: Form a permanent alliance with France against Great Britain.
options.misconception: Washington advised steering clear of permanent alliances, not forming one with France.

options.text: Join Britain in a permanent alliance against France.
options.misconception: Washington advised steering clear of permanent alliances, not joining Britain.

options.text: Steer clear of permanent alliances with any foreign nation.
Refuse all trade with every foreign nation.
options.misconception: Washington warned against political alliances, not against trade.

rationales.C: Washington’s words in the stimulus are to steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world.
rationales.A: Washington advised steering clear of permanent alliances, not forming one with France.
rationales.B: Washington advised steering clear of permanent alliances, not joining Britain.
rationales.D: Washington warned against political alliances, not against trade.
rationales.general:
1. The stimulus quotes Washington directly: steer clear of permanent alliances with any portion of the foreign world.
2. That advice covers every nation, not only France or only Britain.
3. Washington still favored trade; his warning was about political ties that could drag the country into war.
4. So the advice was to avoid permanent alliances, not to ally with one side or stop trading.
Remember: a direct quote answers the question; match the words, not the side you expect.
